predecessors.note: The KIO was founded in 1960 (renamed the Jinghpaw Independence Organization in 1961); its army, the KIA, was reorganised on 5 February 1961 (KIO and KIA pages). Kachin State is the researcher's reading of the area it held.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1961-2023. The Kachin Independence Organization page: 'Aside from its major towns and railway corridor, KIO/A-controlled areas in Kachin State remained virtually independent ... from the mid-1960s through 1994', so the towns and the railway are excluded (Myitkyina, Bhamo, Putao, the Myitkyina-Mogaung-Mohnyin line) and the whole state is no longer drawn. The 1994 ceasefire left the areas in place (the KIA 'lost' jade mines by signing it and has since 'retaken control of most of the jade mines in Hpakant', undated; Kachin Independence Army page); on 2011-2024 that page says 'Fighting continued throughout this period with little real change of borders' and that the KIA is based 'in KIO-held strips of territory' near the Chinese border; it also says the KIA 'took over Kachin Special Region 1 from the New Democratic Army-Kachin' without a date. No page gives an area or a map of the 1995-2023 hold, so one shape stands for all of it. The Chipwi-Panwa area is left out of the zone until the 2024 gain (the KIA 'liberated Chipwi town' on 30 September 2024), which the page implies it did not hold before; for 1961-1994 the pages are silent on it. Soft.

The 30 km Chipwi-Panwa circle returns to the zone, so the shape is Kachin State less the towns and the railway only. The KIA's December 2024 operation on Bhamo took no town. Soft.

notes: Rebel state added by se-04-x; the contest opened in 2011 stays open at the dossier's end (2024). The pages give no area or map, so the zone is Kachin State less its major towns and the railway (see the repair pass below) at soft certainty; a gap-filler should find a source for the KIO's districts (Special Region 1, northern Shan State, the 1994-2011 ceasefire areas) and for the 2024 Panwa and Chipwe positions (Chipwi, Pangwa; no coordinates on any page opened). Dates disagree: the KIO page puts the KIA's reorganisation on 5 February 1961 while the Internal conflict page says it formed after the 1962 coup; the Laiza page does not date the move from Pajau. Pajau has no coordinates on any page (Laiza's are a placeholder). The KIA's takeover of Kachin Special Region 1 from the NDA-K is undated on the KIA page. Page budget: 4 pages. Repair pass 2026-10-25: (1) the reviewer was right that the page excludes the towns and the railway: the zone is now Kachin State minus circles at Myitkyina, Bhamo, Putao, Mogaung, Mohnyin (and a midpoint circle on the Mogaung-Mohnyin line) and the Chipwi-Panwa area, about a seventh smaller than the whole state. Bhamo, Putao, Mohnyin, Mogaung and Chipwi are coordinate circles because the gazetteer lacks them (coordinates printed on their Wikipedia pages are in the sources); the gazetteer agent can swap them for place circles. The railway is three circles, not a line; the gaps between them are small against the 20 km grid cell. (2) 2024: one gain event, 2024-09, for Chipwi and Panwa (confidence 2: the KIO page gives the year only; the Chipwi page gives 30 September 2024 for Chipwi; Panwa is undated and unplaced, as the pages 'Pangwa,_Myanmar', 'Panwa' and 'Pangwa_Township' do not exist and 'Pangwa' is a Tanzanian mountain). I carved the Chipwi circle out of the 1961-2023 zone so the gain is new land; that assumes the area was outside KIO hands before 2024, which the Chipwi page implies for the town ('liberated') but no page says for 1961-1994. (3) Thin item: the page is silent on what the 1994 ceasefire left in KIO hands beyond the jade mines and on the extent in 2011-2024 (it says 'little real change of borders' and 'KIO-held strips of territory' near the Chinese border), so the 1995-2023 shape is the 1961-1994 one.
